mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns higher.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 7% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as investor confidence drops.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 7% but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases (PAYEMS) and unemployment decreases (UNRATE), it indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both employment rises and unemployment falls but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates stimulate economic activity by reducing borrowing costs, leading to increased investments and higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are below 2% but S&P 500 returns do not exceed the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher corporate revenues and thus higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation erodes corporate profit margins and consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If inflation exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP and housing starts increase, it signals strong economic demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns as corporate revenues grow.
failure_condition: If both GDP and housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, high real consumer spending indicates strong demand, supporting higher S&P 500 returns despite potential economic slowdowns elsewhere.
failure_condition: If real consumer spending growth exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns do not beat the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
